title: Per-instance mutable response state is unsafe for overlapping LLM turns
reasoning: The processor stores turn-local data such as _last_response_payload and prompt fingerprints on the shared processor instance. get_response clears _last_response_payload at the start of every call, then later writes the result payload; _resolve_previous_response_id also reads that shared field to wire OpenAI tool-result continuations. If two get_response generators overlap on the same processor, one turn can clear or overwrite another turn's payload, causing get_last_response_payload to return the wrong tool calls or causing an OpenAI tool-result turn to miss/use the wrong previous_response_id. This is a concrete async race because get_response awaits provider streaming between reads and writes of shared mutable state.
reproduction: Start two tasks that iterate the same LLMStreamProcessor.get_response instance concurrently, with one tool-call turn producing a response_id/tool_calls and a second turn starting before the first caller reads get_last_response_payload. The second turn sets _last_response_payload to None at line 114 and can later overwrite it, so the first caller can observe None or the second turn's payload.
recommendation: Keep turn-local response payload in a local variable returned or yielded through the response event path, or serialize get_response calls per processor/session with an async lock. For OpenAI previous_response_id continuation, store continuation state under an explicit conversation/tool-call key instead of a single shared last-payload slot.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: All included tests collect one response at a time from a processor instance; none overlap two get_response async generators or read get_last_response_payload while another turn is in flight.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add an asyncio test with a controlled fake client that blocks mid-stream, starts a second get_response call on the same processor, then resumes both and asserts each caller sees its own payload and previous_response_id state.
minimumFixScope: LLMStreamProcessor response-state ownership and focused async concurrency coverage
